stem: After care, a nurse must discard a contaminated sharp, a dressing saturated enough to release blood if compressed, and unused medication. Which principle is correct?

options.A: Use the applicable separate waste streams: a sharps container for the contaminated sharp, regulated-waste handling for the blood-saturated dressing, and pharmaceutical-waste procedures for the unused medication
options.B: Place all three items in ordinary trash because special disposal applies only to laboratory waste
options.C: Use a sharps container for the needle but place the blood-saturated dressing and unused medication in ordinary trash without further assessment
options.D: Place all three items in one biohazard bag because pharmaceutical waste follows the same rules as every blood-contaminated item

rationale: OSHA defines contaminated sharps and items that would release blood or other potentially infectious material if compressed as regulated waste requiring appropriate containment and disposal. EPA separately requires healthcare facilities to manage pharmaceutical waste under applicable federal, state, and local rules, including RCRA requirements when the pharmaceutical is hazardous waste. A correctly separates these waste categories instead of assuming one universal container. A is correct.
educational_objective: Differentiate sharps, blood-contaminated regulated waste, and pharmaceutical waste disposal streams in healthcare settings.
source_organization: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA); U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
source_document_title: 29 CFR 1910.1030 Bloodborne Pathogens; Information for Hospitals, Pharmacies and Other Businesses that Have Medicines to Dispose
source_version_date: OSHA standard current; EPA page current in 2026, accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: OSHA 1910.1030(d)(4)(iii) regulated waste and contaminated sharps; EPA Healthcare Facilities Must Comply with RCRA section
source_claim_supported: Contaminated sharps and blood-saturated materials meeting OSHA's regulated-waste definition require regulated handling; healthcare-generated pharmaceutical waste is managed under applicable pharmaceutical/hazardous-waste rules rather than a generic clinical-waste stream.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — safe disposal of hazardous/contaminated materials
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — healthcare waste segregation

source_original.stem: A nurse disposes of a used needle, a blood-saturated dressing, and unused medication after care. Which principle is correct?

options.A: Separate sharps, regulated medical, pharmaceutical, and ordinary waste according to applicable rules
options.B: Discard every item in ordinary trash because special waste streams apply only to laboratory material
options.C: Use a sharps container only for needles and place all other clinical waste in ordinary trash
options.D: Place every healthcare item in one biohazard bag because pharmaceutical waste has no separate rules

source_original.rationale: Healthcare waste must be segregated at the point of generation according to the applicable federal, state, local, and facility requirements. Sharps, regulated medical waste, and pharmaceutical or hazardous-drug waste can require different disposal streams.
source_original.source_detail: EPA/OSHA and facility waste rules: segregate sharps, regulated medical, pharmaceutical/hazardous and ordinary waste as applicable; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Made the blood-contaminated dressing meet OSHA's actual regulated-waste threshold rather than treating every bloody dressing identically. Added separate current OSHA and EPA locators and avoided implying that all pharmaceuticals are hazardous waste. Difficulty reduced from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: OSHA regulation plus current EPA healthcare pharmaceutical-waste guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: OSHA standard and EPA 2026 pages checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: OSHA explicitly defines contaminated sharps and releasable-blood materials as regulated waste; EPA states healthcare facilities are responsible for pharmaceutical waste under applicable regulations and RCRA when hazardous.

distractor_audit.C: Incorrectly treats a qualifying blood-saturated dressing and unused medication as ordinary trash by default.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrectly collapses pharmaceutical and bloodborne-pathogen waste rules into one stream.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The stem specifies the OSHA threshold for the dressing and avoids asserting that all medications are hazardous; A is uniquely defensible.
audit_findings.cueing: Options describe competing waste-management approaches without keyword matching.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safe disposal of contaminated materials fits Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked OSHA 1910.1030 and EPA healthcare pharmaceutical disposal; A remains uniquely correct.
